Yes—automatic updates would be reasonable, but the current setup is missing the connection between a Postgkyl merge and website publication. I confirmed two issues:

1. **Postgkyl’s documentation workflow only builds a preview.** It runs on merges to `main`, tests the documentation, and uploads HTML as a GitHub artifact. It never triggers Read the Docs. [Workflow](https://github.com/gkeyllorg/postgkyl/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml)

2. **The separate website repository’s daily publishing trigger is disabled by a missing secret.** Today’s `gkyl-doc` workflow explicitly logged:
   > READTHEDOCS_TOKEN is unset; preview built, hosted refresh skipped.

   That skip still counts as a successful workflow, explaining the green checks without a website update. [Run and logs](https://github.com/gkeyllorg/gkyl-doc/actions/runs/37470557536)

The latest Read the Docs build was **October 2**, before today’s PR merge. Each website build fetches Postgkyl `main`, so a new successful build should pick up your changes. [Latest hosted build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/gkeyll/builds/34900622/)

To fix this:

- **Update now:** manually trigger a Read the Docs build.
- **Enable daily updates:** configure `READTHEDOCS_TOKEN` in `gkyl-doc`.
- **Publish after each merge:** add a Read the Docs build trigger after Postgkyl’s documentation checks pass on `main`.

Configuring the existing secret alone enables daily refreshes; immediate updates require that additional merge trigger.

content.text:
The value of `READTHEDOCS_TOKEN` should be **the API token generated by Read the Docs**, copied exactly. Paste only the token—no quotes, `Token ` prefix, or `READTHEDOCS_TOKEN=`.

1. **Sign in to Read the Docs.**  
   Use an account that can manage builds for the [Gkeyll project](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/gkeyll/). GitHub repository access alone does not grant Read the Docs access. API tokens inherit the permissions of the account that creates them. [Read the Docs authentication documentation](https://docs.readthedocs.com/platform/stable/api/v3.html#authentication-and-authorization)

2. **Generate the token.**  
   Open [Read the Docs → API tokens](https://app.readthedocs.org/accounts/tokens/). Use the option to add a token, give it a descriptive name such as `postgkyl-github-actions`, and copy the generated token.

3. **Open Postgkyl’s GitHub secret settings.**  
   Go directly to [Postgkyl → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions](https://github.com/gkeyllorg/postgkyl/settings/secrets/actions). Select the **Secrets** tab and click **New repository secret**.

4. **Save these values.**

   | Field | What to enter |
   |---|---|
   | Name | `READTHEDOCS_TOKEN` |
   | Secret | The complete token copied from Read the Docs |

   Click **Add secret**. This must be an **Actions repository secret in `gkeyllorg/postgkyl`**. The workflow reads it from there. [GitHub instructions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)

5. **Merge the workflow changes into Postgkyl’s `main`.**  
   The changes I prepared are local. They must reach `main` before automatic publishing works. Adding the secret before merging lets that merge trigger the first hosted build.

6. **Check the publishing trigger.**  
   Open [Postgkyl’s Documentation workflow](https://github.com/gkeyllorg/postgkyl/actions/workflows/docs.yml) and select the run for that merge. After the tests and preview build pass, **Trigger the live Read the Docs build** should print:
   ```text
   Read the Docs build requested: https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/gkeyll/builds/...
   ```
   To retry later, select **Run workflow**, choose **main**, and run it.

7. **Confirm the website build succeeds.**  
   Follow the printed link or open [Gkeyll’s Read the Docs builds](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/gkeyll/builds/). Wait for the new `latest` build to succeed, then check the [development page](https://gkeyll.readthedocs.io/en/latest/postgkyl/development.html). GitHub’s successful trigger means the build was requested; publication happens after Read the Docs finishes.

Keep the token in GitHub’s secret field; do not commit it or paste it into this chat.
